text: The Albinaurics mutter that the stars will punish the world in flame, speaking to those who have forsaken them.
On the third day of an expedition, the Erdtree is absent entirely, and Limgrave has become distorted and at risk of disappearing due to the Night Lord's power over fate.
The underground crypt beneath the Round Table Hold contains eight coffins, seemingly corresponding to the eight playable Nightfarer characters.
The Sacred Tree, coiled around a divine tower, is the location where players fight at the end of each day in Nightreign, serving as the last bastion against the Night.
At the end of the second night, the Sacred Tree beckons the Nightfarers upward into a white tower called the Spirit Shelter, known in Japanese as the Sacred Tree.
Unlike other great trees in Elden Ring lore, the Sacred Tree in Nightreign is not physically rooted to one place, but appears wherever it is needed, since it is a spiritual manifestation.
The Round Table Hold functions as a refuge outside of time and space that Nightfarers return to between expeditions.
Ruins explored by Night Farers in Limveld are physical remnants of the pre-catastrophe civilization, including still-standing roads, cathedral outlines, and flickering sites of grace.
Unlike classic hollowing in the Dark Souls trilogy and base Elden Ring, which is a gradual erosion of self from lost grace, the Forsaken Hollows were suddenly and deliberately cut off from grace.

The Round Table Hold appears in Limveld in a recognizable but empty, evacuated form rather than one gradually abandoned, with displaced objects, open doors, an open book, and unfinished equipment modifications suggesting a hurried departure.
The Round Table Hold is the place where the Nightfarers stay, plan, and train to fight the Night Lord.
Inscriptions in the crypt reference the Deep Woods (home of the Recluse) and Wind Whale Null (home of the Wilder and Duchess).
Nokstella, the Shrouded City, is one of the new locations introduced in Nightreign.
In-game text refers to Nokstella as an 'Eternal City,' once part of a greater whole.
